topicName: Cell Structure and Organization of Life
description: This topic explores the cell as the basic structural and functional unit of life, the use of the light microscope, differences between plant and animal cells, the functions of cell organelles, and how cells build up tissues, organs, systems and whole organisms.

mcq.questionText: What is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things?
mcq.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all the activities of life, so it is the basic unit of structure and function in organisms.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is most commonly used in a Form 1 laboratory to view cells that are too small to see with the naked eye?
mcq.explanation: The light microscope uses lenses and light to magnify tiny specimens such as cells, making them visible to the observer.

mcq.questionText: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
mcq.explanation: Only plant cells have a rigid cellulose cell wall outside the cell membrane; animal cells lack a cell wall.

mcq.questionText: Which organelle controls the activities of the cell and contains the genetic material?
mcq.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes (genetic material) and directs all the activities of the cell, acting like its control centre.

mcq.questionText: Which organelle is the main site of energy release (respiration) in the cell?
mcq.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, releasing energy from food for the cell to use.

mcq.questionText: The green pigment in chloroplasts that traps light energy for photosynthesis is called:
mcq.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment inside chloroplasts that absorbs light energy used to make food during photosynthesis.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the cell controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell?
mcq.explanation: The cell membrane is partially permeable and regulates which substances enter or leave the cell.

mcq.questionText: On a light microscope, which part is turned to bring the specimen into sharp focus under high power?
mcq.explanation: The fine adjustment knob makes small, precise movements of the lens to sharpen the image, especially under high power.

mcq.questionText: A large, permanent, fluid-filled vacuole that helps keep the cell firm is a typical feature of:
mcq.explanation: Mature plant cells have one large permanent vacuole containing cell sap that keeps the cell turgid and firm.

mcq.questionText: Which sequence correctly shows the levels of organization from simplest to most complex?
mcq.explanation: Cells group into tissues, tissues form organs, organs work together as systems, and systems make up the whole organism.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an organ in the human body?
mcq.explanation: The heart is an organ made of several tissues working together to pump blood around the body.

mcq.questionText: Why is a thin specimen prepared on a slide before viewing under a light microscope?

options.text: To allow light to pass through it

mcq.explanation: A thin specimen lets light pass through so the structures inside the cells can be seen clearly.

mcq.questionText: The jelly-like material where many chemical reactions of the cell take place is the:
mcq.explanation: Cytoplasm is the watery, jelly-like substance that holds the organelles and where many cell reactions occur.

mcq.questionText: A stain such as iodine or methylene blue is added to a specimen mainly to:

options.text: Make cell structures easier to see

mcq.explanation: Stains colour certain parts of the cell so that structures such as the nucleus stand out clearly under the microscope.

mcq.questionText: A group of similar cells working together to perform a particular function is called a/an:
mcq.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells specialised to carry out the same function, for example muscle tissue.

fib.questionText: The smallest unit that can carry out all the activities of life is the _____.
fib.explanation: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in all living organisms.

fib.questionText: The rigid layer made of cellulose found only outside plant cells is the _____.
fib.explanation: The cellulose cell wall gives plant cells shape and support and is absent in animal cells.

fib.questionText: The organelle that controls all the activities of the cell is the _____.
fib.explanation: The nucleus contains the genetic material and acts as the control centre of the cell.

fib.questionText: The green pigment found in chloroplasts that traps light energy is called _____.
fib.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy used by the plant to make food during photosynthesis.

fib.questionText: Energy is released from food during respiration mainly in organelles called _____.
fib.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration where energy is released for cell activities.

fib.questionText: The partially permeable structure that controls what enters and leaves the cell is the _____.
fib.explanation: The cell membrane regulates the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

fib.questionText: A group of similar cells that work together to do the same job is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Tissues are made of similar cells specialised for a common function.

fib.questionText: Different organs that work together to perform a major task form an organ _____.
fib.explanation: An organ system, such as the digestive system, is made of several organs working together.

fib.questionText: Before viewing on a microscope, a glass cover slip is lowered onto the specimen to avoid trapping _____.
fib.explanation: Lowering the cover slip slowly prevents air bubbles, which can be mistaken for cell structures.

fib.questionText: The total magnification of a microscope is found by multiplying the eyepiece magnification by the _____ magnification.
fib.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece magnification multiplied by the objective lens magnification in use.

tf.questionText: All living organisms are made up of one or more cells.
tf.explanation: The cell theory states that all living things are made of cells, whether unicellular or multicellular.

tf.questionText: Animal cells have a cell wall made of cellulose.
tf.explanation: Only plant cells have a cellulose cell wall; animal cells are bounded only by a cell membrane.

tf.questionText: Chloroplasts are found in most animal cells.
tf.explanation: Chloroplasts are present in green plant cells, not in animal cells, because animals do not photosynthesise.

tf.questionText: The nucleus contains the cell's genetic material.
tf.explanation: The nucleus holds chromosomes that carry the hereditary information of the cell.

tf.questionText: Mitochondria are responsible for storing genetic information in the cell.
tf.explanation: Mitochondria release energy through respiration; the nucleus stores the genetic information.

tf.questionText: A mature plant cell usually has one large permanent vacuole.
tf.explanation: Mature plant cells contain a single large vacuole filled with cell sap that keeps the cell firm.

tf.questionText: Tissues are simpler in organization than cells.
tf.explanation: Cells are simpler; tissues are made up of many similar cells and are therefore more complex.

tf.questionText: A light microscope uses light and lenses to magnify small specimens.
tf.explanation: The light microscope passes light through a thin specimen and uses lenses to enlarge the image.

tf.questionText: The cell membrane allows all substances to pass freely into and out of the cell.
tf.explanation: The cell membrane is partially (selectively) permeable, allowing only certain substances to pass through.

tf.questionText: Increasing the objective lens power on a microscope increases the total magnification of the specimen.
tf.explanation: Total magnification is the eyepiece power times the objective power, so a higher objective gives greater magnification.

summary.correctAnswer: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things.
summary.explanation: Everything an organism does ultimately happens at the level of cells.

summary.correctAnswer: The nucleus controls cell activities and stores the genetic material.
summary.explanation: It directs growth, repair and reproduction by controlling the cell's processes.

summary.correctAnswer: Mitochondria release energy from food through respiration.
summary.explanation: They are often called the powerhouse of the cell because they supply usable energy.

summary.correctAnswer: Chloroplasts trap light energy and make food during photosynthesis.
summary.explanation: They contain the green pigment chlorophyll and are found only in green plant cells.

summary.correctAnswer: The cell membrane controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
summary.explanation: It is partially permeable, letting only certain substances pass.

summary.questionText: Plant cell features absent in animal cells
summary.correctAnswer: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole are found in plant cells but not animal cells.
summary.explanation: These features support the plant and allow it to make its own food.

summary.correctAnswer: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like material that holds organelles and where many reactions occur.
summary.explanation: It provides a medium for the chemical activities of the cell.

summary.questionText: Levels of organization in living things
summary.correctAnswer: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism, from simplest to most complex.
summary.explanation: Each level is built from the level below it.

summary.correctAnswer: The light microscope magnifies tiny specimens using light and lenses so cells can be seen.
summary.explanation: Total magnification equals eyepiece power times objective power.

summary.correctAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform the same function.
summary.explanation: Examples include muscle tissue and xylem tissue.

hoq.questionText: A student looks at two cells under a microscope. Cell X has a cell wall, chloroplasts and one large vacuole, while Cell Y has none of these but has a membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus. What is the best conclusion?

options.text: Cell X is a plant cell and Cell Y is an animal cell
Cell X is an animal cell and Cell Y is a plant cell

hoq.explanation: A cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole are typical of plant cells (X), while their absence indicates an animal cell (Y).

hoq.questionText: A muscle cell is described as having many more mitochondria than an ordinary skin cell. What does this suggest about the muscle cell?

options.text: It needs to make its own food by photosynthesis
It requires a large amount of energy for its work
It does not need any energy

hoq.explanation: Mitochondria release energy, so a cell with many mitochondria, like a muscle cell, has a high energy demand for its activities such as contraction.

hoq.questionText: A microscope has an eyepiece of magnification x10 and the student switches from the x4 objective to the x40 objective. How does the total magnification change?
hoq.explanation: Total magnification is eyepiece times objective, so it changes from 10 x 4 = 40 to 10 x 40 = 400.
